stem: A team's database credentials currently live in a flat configuration file with no automatic rotation, and separately, its multi-step order workflow is coordinated by custom retry code the team wrote and must keep maintaining. Which TWO managed services replace this self-managed work? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store standard parameters, configured to rotate the credentials automatically
AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation configured for the database credentials
Amazon EventBridge invoking a Lambda function on a fixed schedule to advance the workflow to its next step
AWS Secrets Manager storing the credentials, with automatic rotation left turned off
AWS Step Functions coordinating the multi-step order workflow as a state machine

rationale: AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation configured replaces the flat configuration file that has no rotation at all. AWS Step Functions coordinates a multi-step workflow as a state machine instead of the custom orchestration and retry code the team would otherwise have to write and maintain, replacing the second self-managed piece. Systems Manager Parameter Store standard parameters store values but do not rotate them automatically, so configuring them to do so is not something the service supports; it does not replace the rotation the team needs. An EventBridge rule invoking a Lambda function on a fixed schedule only triggers the next step at set intervals; it still leaves the team to write and maintain the logic that tracks workflow state and retries failures, rather than replacing that orchestration outright. Secrets Manager with rotation left turned off is the right service for storing the credentials, but without rotation enabled it does not solve the 'no automatic rotation' problem the team has today.
